implementation_summary: Sink-path handlers added beside legacy ones: poll 10/11/12, profile 0, profile-request 30 (assertPorts-validated), chat takes injected groupOf (live group.members()/admins via groupGates.ts; undefined fails closed, rejection rejects the row; legacy path keeps catch-false). Retract for every kind: chat carrier removal + recomputeUnread (new unreadStore.recomputeUnread, shared predicate with initUnreadCounts, exact semantics), own chat -> onOwnWithdrawn; reactions held until target lands (holdReaction/releaseHeldReactions, released after every kind-9 delivery) and retractReaction; delete/edit signals recompute their slot on retract (write-once ChatMessage.original base, reset, refold of the remaining rows); poll retractPollOpen/Vote/Close. Follow-up writes (profile-request replies, accepted announcement) enqueued on the FIFO as the last action. GroupRumorInput.reason 'purged' makes a late retract after leave remove an own row instead of failed/retry. handlersRumorPubkeyBoundary re-expressed behaviourally (sender != rumor pubkey). GATE REMEDIATION (Fable ruling): incremental-undo retracts replaced by recompute-on-retract. Sink: HistoryRow.receivedAt (first append) and withdrawing marks (mark all, retract all, delete all; recovery/sweep finish marked rows before any re-dispatch; a live re-append of a marked id finishes it first); RetractInput.remaining() = dispatched && !withdrawing rows in seq order, memoised per batch, also on the late-retract path. Stores: recomputeSlot (write-once ChatMessage.original base, shared foldClassifiedSignal core, pins re-derived from receivedAt, (rumorId, author) identity), recomputeMessageReactions (shared foldInboundRumor, sender-scoped dedup, own unconfirmed optimistic rows carried over, re-hold when target absent), recomputePoll (pollCore shared by dispatch and an effect-free in-memory fold in pollFold, receivedAt receipt clock). Handlers derive the aggregate key, call remainingSignals + the store, bump. Base-message last carrier withdrawn recomputes its slot and reactions with the target absent. Independent findings fixed: profile sink gate keyed per group (bounded 1024); accepted announcement: marker consumed as the last step and the announcement enqueued as the last action (finally); unread recompute tracks reads during the reconcile and keeps the count on a read failure; held reactions per-sender cap, sender-matched removal, purgeHeldReactionsForGroup.

verification.unit_full: make test-unit: tsc -p tsconfig.tests-marmot.json clean; 331 files, 7363 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (after examiner remediation)

decisions: Purge-after-leave: chose a retract reason (GroupRumorInput.reason 'purged', absent=withdrawn) over ordering leave cleanup; only the purge late-retract sets it; chat purged retract removes the row via removeMessages, own rows included.
Reactions are held (bounded queue: 7 d TTL, 200/thread, deduped by rumor id) and released after every kind-9 delivery; dispatch re-checks after holding to close the race.
Profile (0) and profile-request (30) retract are deliberate no-ops: LWW identity metadata / already-emitted replies (AC-WDR-6). Profile is not roster-gated (profileSync exempts it by design).
profile-request gate: requester must be a live current member; own request echo is ignored; replies enqueue on the FIFO.
Kind 13 is retired in kinds.ts: no sink handler; leaveHandler.ts stays legacy-only until S22; leave announcement is the kind-9 leave_intent gate in chat.

messageEdits withdraw is recompute-on-retract, not an undo: the slot is reset to the row's write-once `original` (captured for every group-thread write) and the remaining kind-5/9 rows are refolded in seq order through the same fold core as dispatch (recomputeSlot); pending entries are re-buffered with the folded row's receivedAt (deterministic under any wall clock, AC-WDR-9). A group-thread signal without an authenticated sender throws (never falls back to rumor.pubkey); the local account's own optimistic send passes itself as sender.

Poll retract is recompute-on-retract: the remaining kind-10/11/12 rows naming the poll are refolded in seq order into the poll's stores in one transaction (recomputePoll / pollFold, receivedAt receipt clock), so a withdrawn open, vote or close needs no per-kind undo rule; a close re-opens only when no remaining creator close exists, and a poll group handler requires the held close-announcement replay port at construction (the legacy factory may omit it).
AC-HIST-12: legacy suites stay on the legacy factories until S22; sink-path equivalents added per kind plus behavioural boundary tests.
Recompute-on-retract per the Fable ruling; RemainingRow.receivedAt falls back to rumor.created_at*1000 for rows written before receivedAt existed (deterministic, keeps the number type).
Withdraw marks before first-touch recovery; recovery finishes OTHER marked rows (an earlier interrupted batch) and never re-dispatches marked rows; the batch itself is finished by the withdraw.

Profile accepted announcement: consumePendingDirectInviteMarker moved to the handler's last step and the enqueue to the dispatch call's finally, honouring the ClientJobQueue last-action rule (an earlier enqueue mid-handler would risk reentrant). A throw of consumePendingDirectInviteMarker propagates (the row stays undispatched, the sink retries it, the marker is still present, the retry announces once).

Carrier sender binding: appendOrAddCarrier compares message.senderPubkey (= the authenticated sender the handler builds the row from) to the stored row's sender instead of taking a separate sender argument; addMessageCarrier takes an optional sender for the same check.

Withdraw is incremental (retract then delete per row, per-step settle bound; leftover marked rows are finished at the start of the next append/withdraw of the group, tracked in memory); aggregate dedupe lives in createGroupRumorDispatch via GroupKindHandler.retractKey + the batch's shared remaining() function, and RetractInput.batch carries the whole withdrawn set (pins of every batch row go with the one recompute).

One clock: GroupRumorInput.receivedAt (row's persisted first-append time) drives applyDeleteEditSignal's classification (options.receivedAt) and the poll receipt stamps (receiptNow(atLeast) port); recomputeMessageReactions' doc now says the wall clock is read only for the held queue's heldAt bookkeeping.

Reaction rows keep id = rumor id; identity is scoped instead: optimisticAddRows matches by (id, reactor), rollbackOptimistic matches only the in-flight (eventId '') row, optionally pinned to a reactor.
Slot base capture: ChatMessage.original is captured for every group-thread signal write (sink-delivered and own optimistic, so AC-WDR-2 holds for own edits/deletes), never for DM threads.
limitations: No production wiring yet (S6/S18): groupOf, enqueue, onOwnEcho/onOwnWithdrawn, recomputeUnread(ownPubkey), registerGroupAdminsProvider(createGroupAdminsProvider(groupOf)), holdReaction ports.
Withdrawn profile does not restore the previous profile.
Live-state gates (admin delete of an announcement) are re-evaluated against the live roster at recompute, failing closed (accepted residual, documented in each store).

Slot oracle equivalence is modulo ghost pending entries: a multi-e-tag delete buffers entries for prior-replacement ids that never become rows; their survival depends on arrival history (tests strip only those).

Held poll votes are keyed by poll id: if the original open is withdrawn and another member already opened the same poll id, the oracle (and recompute) apply the held votes to that poll; the creator binding only stops the original creator's close.
A recompute does not re-gate already-accepted poll_close chat announcements (kind 9) against a changed tally.
An optimistic removal of an already-confirmed own reaction reverts to the live add during a recompute until its echo is folded.
Accepted announcement: a hard kill between the marker commit and the synchronous enqueue (no await in between) can still lose it; no persisted pending-announcement record.

A withdrawing row whose retract keeps failing or times out stays marked (hidden from remaining()/list()) while the rows before it are already deleted (incremental progress); the next append/withdraw of the group in the same instance, first-touch recovery after a restart, or sweep finishes the rest.

A recompute that runs while a row of the group is still dispatched:false (undispatched, recovering, abandoned) does not see it in remaining(): that row's effects are reset by the recompute and applied again when the row is (re-)dispatched (accepted; documented in the GroupHistoryHandlers seam and the historyBackend doc).

Production wiring owes two new ports: PollGroupHandlerDeps.receiptNow (pollPersistence.receiptNow(atLeast)) and the 4th selfPubkeyHex argument of recomputePoll; handlers fall back to the wall clock only for an input without receivedAt (hand-built inputs).
Withdraw dedupe is per aggregate: plain kind-9 retracts (carrier accounting, recomputeUnread) still run per row; a batch of many withdrawn plain messages repeats the unread recompute per row.

A hung (timed-out) retract may still complete after its call was abandoned and overwrite a newer recompute of the same aggregate with its older snapshot (pre-existing residual of the abandon model; the store serialises, it does not version).

A forged byte-identical copy of a kind-9 message whose real sender's delivery is withdrawn leaves no row (the copy's own history row is not re-applied as the forger's message): plain kind-9 rows keep carrier accounting outside the AC-WDR-7 oracle.

Recovered out-of-seq dispatch: a dependent row whose first dispatch failed and is recovered after later rows is applied live after them (receiptNow high-water mark), while the fold places it at its seq/receivedAt; live and fold re-converge at the next recompute of that aggregate (accepted residual).

A retract that outlives its per-row 10 s bound keeps running with the batch's memoised remaining(); a row of the same aggregate dispatched meanwhile can be reset until the next recompute of that aggregate (needs a >10 s retract; accepted residual).

Plain kind-9 forged copies: a byte-identical copy by another member registers no carrier and stores no effect; when the real author's entry is withdrawn the row is removed and the copy is not re-applied as the copier's message (attribution-safe; AC-WDR-7 exempts plain kind-9).

Forger-first plain kind-9 copy: if a byte-identical copy from another member were delivered before the author's, the row would carry the first deliverer's sender and its withdraw would remove the row - unreachable through the library, which binds rumor.pubkey to the MLS sender and drops such forgeries at receive (forgery.harness.test.ts); defence-in-depth only.
Legacy behavioural suites still exercise the legacy factories until S22 deletes them (sink-path equivalents exist).

A recompute re-buffers pending delete/edit entries with the folded row's receivedAt: a row older than the pending TTL re-buffers an entry the next thread activity's sweep may already expire (deterministic by design, AC-WDR-9).

decisions_needed.question: When a poll-open is withdrawn while another member's open for the same poll id remains, should votes cast for the original be applied to the surviving poll (current: yes, same as live dispatch, held votes are keyed by poll id)?
decisions_needed.default: Keep current behaviour (matches dispatch-only-remaining oracle); bind held votes to the creator only if product wants it.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The recompute oracle compares aux state (pending signals, markers, held queues) that is order-dependent in ways the ruling did not anticipate: tombstone-hidden content and ghost pending entries for never-row ids differed by arrival path and were found only by seeded property loops. Parallel workers on shared fixtures (realApp.ts) also broke each other's runs for minutes.
retrospective.surprised_by: realApp nextGroupId wrapped at 256 and could equal fixed account pubkeys (aa..), silently corrupting textual group-id normalisation in oracle snapshots; fixed with a non-wrapping 4-hex counter.
